observed: Eight distinct traders appear from the front and back, with a small trading station and stool at one end.
A still veteran, raised-slip hustler, running trader, hunched phone caller, plane thrower, tired trader, paper-clutching newcomer and taller bell ringer have different lines of action.
Rolled sleeves, braces, ties, jackets and a jacket over the shoulder vary the clothing and silhouette.
Rounded heads and natural head tones replace the rejected cube-headed mannequin shape.
corrections: The chest emblem is not gold; use the Atlas emblem material once picked.
No jacket colour sits near brass, which is reserved for live readings.
A paper-plane throw keeps a curled wrist so it never reads as a salute.
The shouting pose has no mouth; posture carries the mood.
Heads are a little larger than in the references so they read at 40 pixels; the exact ratio still needs a pick.
Remove the voice's gold lapel pin and the night-shift trader's mouth-marking goatee; retain personality through body and simple hair shapes.
Do not copy brass bell brackets or stands as decoration, or treat realistic head ratios and textured shading as final geometry or materials.

Colour audit 13 October: add timber support in the realized scene; the sheet only has page ground, not a sampled floor. Lift darkest jacket/timber faces for 3:1 near-black outlines, simplify gradients and remove station writing; retain the existing non-gold emblem and no-brass-like-jacket corrections.
